device.name: Antelope Orion Studio Synergy Core
device.notes: Composite USB device; control is entirely via the vendor HID interface (iface 3). UAC2 audio-control interface has no Feature Units. Model lineage (for disambiguation): this is the 2020 'Orion Studio Synergy Core' -- the third Orion Studio generation, after the 2015 Orion Studio and the 2017 Orion Studio Rev.2017. Not the same as the Orion 32 / Orion 32+ / Orion HD (the multichannel converters). The device reports its own name as 'OrionStudio_III' in readback category 0x01, hence the file's old name orion_studio_3.json (renamed to orion_studio_sc.json 2026-09-03, matching the *_sc.json Synergy Core family naming -- zen_go_sc, discrete_8_pro_sc, discrete_4_sc, discrete_4_pro_sc).

transport.notes: Confirmed from raw pcapng (2026-08): the vendor control protocol is entirely HID interrupt on interface 3, endpoint 0x01 OUT / 0x82 IN, device address 2 (usb.dst 1.2.x). Endpoints 0x05 OUT / 0x84 IN are the UAC2 isochronous audio stream (24-ch / 24-bit in the class-compliant descriptor) -- unrelated to control. Only 16 USB control transfers in the whole connect sequence: standard descriptor GETs + SET_CONFIGURATION/SET_INTERFACE, NO string-descriptor fetches in any capture on file. The UAC2 audio-control descriptor is a stub (1 clock source, 4 terminals all nrChannels=1, no Feature Units), so it carries no usable channel topology or names.
transport.hidraw_write_length_unverified: The sibling Antelope Discrete 8 Pro (peer PR, profile discrete_8_pro_sc.json) has a HID report descriptor with NO Report ID item, so on Linux hidraw a write there must be 321 bytes (leading 0x00 report-number byte + 320-byte payload), NOT 320. This CLI's transport.py currently writes exactly 320 bytes for Orion with no prefix, and the confirmed params suggest that works here -- but it has not been checked against Orion's actual descriptor. Verify with: cat /sys/class/hidraw/hidrawN/device/report_descriptor and look for a Report ID item (0x85 ...). If Orion's descriptor also lacks one, transport.py needs the leading 0x00 for Orion too. Discrete 8 Pro's full descriptor, for comparison: 06 a0 ff 09 01 a1 01 09 02 a1 00 06 a1 ff 09 03 09 04 15 80 25 7f 35 00 45 ff 75 08 96 40 01 81 02 09 05 09 06 15 80 25 7f 35 00 45 ff 75 08 96 40 01 91 02 c0 c0 (no 0x85).

command.notes: The general-purpose 'set one param for one target' frame. Used for every per-input-channel param (gain, mode, phantom, phase), the per-bus params (bus_level/bus_dim/bus_mute/bus_mono) and talkback_dest_assign. channel_offset means different things depending on the param: a physical input index (0-11) for channel params, a bus id (0-5, all six now identified -- see 'buses') for bus params, or a talkback destination index (0-3) for talkback_dest_assign. No known GET/query opcode -- state is read passively from IN reports. magic (byte 0) 0x70 is written for family consistency; on the sibling Discrete 8 Pro byte 0 is IGNORED on outgoing commands (offset 4 / opcode is the real discriminator there), and that most likely holds for Orion too -- byte 0 as 'the magic' is a property of the INCOMING reports (0x73/0x75/0x74), not the outgoing command.

space_values.3: virtual-mixer channel link (Mix 1-4 strips) -- CONFIRMED macos-mix1-send-pan-fader-mute-solo-link (2026-08): linking mix ch1+ch2 sent SET_LINK space=0x03 pair_index=0x00 enabled=0x01. Software-mirrored like the other link spaces -- while linked the Launcher re-sent BOTH strips' mix_command frames on every fader move.
space_values.4: AFX-tab channel stereo-link -- 32 channels -> 16 pairs, pair_index = channel_index // 2. CONFIRMED macos-afx-stereolink-1-2_3-4_5-6_27-28_29-30_31-32 (2026-09-04, scanned in ../antelope-ctl-afx): the AFX tab stereo-link buttons for pairs 0/1/2 (ch 1-2, 3-4, 5-6) and 13/14/15 (ch 27-28, 29-30, 31-32) each sent ONE bare `a2 04 <pair> <en>` frame -- nothing past [19], NO partner gain-sync frame (there is no per-channel gain here, unlike the preamp link -- just the flag), NO readback (the 0x73 deltas in that capture are meter jitter, uncorrelated with the link toggles; no 0x74 at all). Bucket A/B -- a channel-pairing toggle, not plugin-internal. Buildable via build_link_command(profile, pair, enabled, space=4); no dedicated CLI command.

link_command.notes: A SEPARATE frame shape from the SET_PARAM command -- do NOT build it with build_command()/build_raw_command(). param_id at 16 lines up with SET_PARAM's. Offset 17 was previously thought unused/always-0; capture spdif-gain-link (2026-08) shows it is a SPACE/DOMAIN selector: 0x00 for physical + ADAT link (which still can't be told apart from each other -- both use 0x00), 0x01 for S/PDIF link, 0x03 for the virtual mixer, 0x04 for the AFX tab. pair_index is at 18, explicit enabled 0/1 at 19. Confirmed: chlink (all 6 physical pairs, space 0), ADAT-link1-2-7-8 (pairs 0/1/6/7, space 0), spdif-gain-link (pair 0, space 1), mix link (space 3, macos-mix1-...), AFX stereo-link (space 4, macos-afx-stereolink-...).

routing_command.addressable_destinations_note: ALL 15 destination groups are now writable (2026-09-01). The first six are physical outputs; 6-14 are internal or digital and were left unwired until their channel counts were confirmed off the cat-0x03 readback. Each was live-read before wiring and the counts matched destination_channels exactly: com_rec 32, adat_out 16, spdif_out 2, afx_in 32, mix_ch1-4 32 each, surround_in 16. NOTE mix_chN (10-13) is the input side of the VIRTUAL MIXER: its 32 channels are what each of mix N's 32 strips listens to, so `route mix1 5 preamp3` chooses strip 5's source and `mix-set 1 5 --fader ...` sets that same strip's level -- two halves of one signal path (frame.mix_command, readback cat 0x04).
routing_command.destination_channels_note: All 15 CONFIRMED 2026-08-31 by the routing readback (frame.readback category 0x03): each record is <dest_id> + destination_channels[dest_id] (bank,idx) pairs. line_out 16, hp1/hp2/mona/monb/reamp/spdif_out 2, comp_rec/afx_in/mix_ch1..4 32, adat_out/surround_in 16.
routing_command.channel_addressing: The CLI addresses an output channel 1-based: `route <dest> <N> <source>` sets channel N (1..destination_channels[dest]) of that group. For stereo_destinations (hp1/hp2/mona/monb) `L` = channel 1 and `R` = channel 2 are accepted aliases. Reamp is NOT a stereo pair (Reamp 1 / Reamp 2 are separate mono outs) so use 1/2 there. `route <dest> all <s1> <s2> ...` sets every channel at once; `route <dest> mute` mutes all; `route <dest> <N> mute` mutes one.
routing_command.frame_model: CORRECTED 2026-08 (captures macos-matrix-ch1-12-mute-hp1L / -hp1R). The frame is `d3 41 <dest> | <bank0> <idx0> | <bank1> <idx1> | ...` -- after destination_offset (18) it is a plain array of (source_bank, source_index) pairs, one per output channel of the destination GROUP, starting at channel_list_offset (19) with channel_stride (2). Channel 0 = L / output 1 / Reamp 1; channel 1 = R / output 2 / Reamp 2. Multichannel groups (line_out, adat_out=16, ...) simply have more pairs. mute = mute_source (bank 0x0b, idx 0); there is no 'no source' encoding. THE WHOLE GROUP IS ALWAYS SENT -- there is no single-channel frame. EVIDENCE: hp1L capture swept preamp 1-12 into HP1 L; every frame was `d3 41 01 | 00 (n-1) | 00 02` -- [19][20] = the changing L source, [21][22] = (0x00,0x02) = preamp 3, HP1 R's unchanged source. hp1R capture then swept preamp 1-12 into HP1 R; every frame was `d3 41 01 | 0b 00 | 00 (n-1)` -- [19][20] = (0x0b,0) = MUTE (HP1 L, left muted by hp1L's final frame), [21][22] = the changing R source. The two captures are sequential and the L=mute state carries between them -- decisive. Final mutes: hp1L -> `d3 41 01 | 0b 00 | 00 02` (mute L, keep R); hp1R -> `d3 41 01 | 0b 00 | 0b 00` (mute both).
routing_command.supersedes: This REPLACES the old op1_offset/op2_offset/output_ops model (bytes 21-22 = '02 01' for output 1, '00 02' for output 2). That was a misread: '00 02' is literally (bank 0x00, index 0x02) = preamp 3, i.e. the OTHER channel's untouched routing, not an opcode. The old CLI shipped this bug -- `route hp1 R preamp4` wrote preamp4 to [20] (the L slot) and preamp3 to [21][22] (R), so it set L=preamp4, R=preamp3 (user-observed on the Windows Launcher, 2026-08).
routing_command.mono_matrix: The routing matrix treats EVERY output channel independently (user-confirmed 2026-08). HP1 L and HP1 R are separate array slots; no stereo-pair concept.
routing_command.multichannel_channel_counts: Output-channel counts per destination group (the frame carries one (bank,index) pair per channel, all sent every time): hp1/hp2/mona/monb=2, reamp=2, spdif_out=2; LINE_OUT=16 (CONFIRMED 2026-08 -- macos-matrix-afx*/surrnd*/mix1234* frames end at byte 50 = 16 pairs at bytes 19-50; caveat: a trailing channel routed to (bank 0, idx 0) would read as 00 00 and be invisible, but 16 matches the Launcher matrix). Still unknown: com_rec, adat_out (16 from the old adat_out '15x 03 NN' note), afx_in, mix_ch1..4, surround_in. Only the 2-channel groups are wired into the CLI so far. In the confirmed line_out captures, byte 18 = 0x00 and channel 0 was the one being changed; channels 1-15 held their prior routing (preamp 2-12 then compplay 1-4).

The DSP is controlled by micmodeling_command (opcode 0x17 / param 0xe5). CONFIRMED 2026-08-31 from capture 'emumic-5to 12' (Windows KVM): routed emumic into line_out ch 1-8, one channel at a time -> pairs (0x01, 0) .. (0x01, 7). So bank 0x01 has 8 indices, 0-7. The Launcher labels them by PREAMP NUMBER 5-12 (idx 0 = preamp 5), even though the front-panel EMU button only appears on preamps 7-12 -- so emumic idx 0-1 (preamps 5-6) are selectable as matrix sources with no way to configure a model on them (a Launcher bug or an unfinished feature; UNTESTED whether the card actually produces audio on those two taps). CLI source spec: emumicN with N = preamp number 5-12 -> (0x01, N-5).

source_banks.0x07: mix 2 -- virtual mix 2, idx 0/1 = L/R. CONFIRMED (same capture).
source_banks.0x08: mix 3 -- virtual mix 3, idx 0/1 = L/R. CONFIRMED (same capture).

routing_command.cli_support: CLI `route` / `matrix-status`. `route <dest> <chan> <source>` sets ONE output channel (1-based; `L`/`R` = 1/2 for stereo_destinations) -- the other channels are read live from the device first (frame.readback cat 0x03) and every write is read back and confirmed. `route <dest> all <s1> <s2> ...` sets the whole group; `route <dest> mute` mutes all; `route <dest> <chan> mute` mutes one. `matrix-status` is a full live read of all 15 groups. Like the Launcher there is NO un-route. Source specs: preamp N -> (0x00,N-1); emumic N (N = preamp number 5-12) -> (0x01,N-5); compplay N (alias playback) -> (0x02,N-1); adat N -> (0x03,N-1); spdif L|R -> (0x04,0|1); afx N -> (0x05,N-1); mix1..4 L|R -> (0x06..0x09, 0|1); surround N -> (0x0a,N-1); osc N -> (0x0c,N-1); mute -> mute_source. Dests wired: ALL 15 (2026-09-01). line_out 16, hp1/hp2/mona/monb/reamp/spdif_out 2, adat_out/surround_in 16, com_rec/afx_in/mix_ch1-4 32. Names accept the ids in addressable_destinations (com_rec, adat_out, spdif_out, afx_in, mix_ch1..mix_ch4, surround_in). spdif_out is in stereo_destinations so L/R work there too.
routing_command.notes: The matrix/routing frame -- its own command shape (opcode 0x53, NOT the SET_PARAM layout). [16]=0xd3, [17]=0x41 (constant), [18]=destination group. After that: an array of (source_bank, source_index) pairs, one per output channel of the group, from channel_list_offset (19), stride 2 -- see frame_model. Source banks in source_banks. Destination map from capture matrix-compplay-allouts-1: 0=line_out 1=hp1 2=hp2 3=mona 4=monb 5=reamp 6=com_rec 7=adat_out 8=spdif_out 9=afx_in 10-13=mix_ch1..4 14=surround_in. Routing is EXCLUSIVE per channel (one source per output channel; 'virtual mixes' are the separate summing mechanism). NO USB readback at all -- see params.routing.readback (HID descriptor has no Feature report; device STALLs GET_REPORT; preset-load is pure push).

global_command.notes: A third command shape, for device-global params that have no per-channel/per-bus target. Same header as SET_PARAM but the single value byte sits at offset 17 (where SET_PARAM keeps its channel byte); offset 18 is unused/0. Confirmed from the talkback captures (2026-08): talkback_button (param 0x1f), talkback_source (param 0x27) and talkback_gain (param 0x20) all use opcode 0x12 with the value at offset 17. Build with build_global_command(profile, param_id, value) -- NOT build_command() (which would put the value at offset 18).

mix_command.notes: Opcode 0x17 with param_id [16]=0xd4 -- the VIRTUAL MIXER (the Mix 1-4 windows, a SEPARATE UI from the routing matrix: mixing happens here, then Mix N's L/R appear as sources in the matrix, banks 0x06-0x09). NOTE opcode 0x17 is SHARED: param_id 0xe5 on the same opcode is mic modeling (frame.micmodeling_command) -- always check [16]. One frame per (mix, channel) strip, carrying that strip's WHOLE state every time. CONFIRMED from macos-mix1-send-pan-fader-mute-solo-link (2026-08, native macOS): [16]=0xd4 [17]=0x05 constant; [18]=mix number 0-3 (0 = Mix 1 .. 3 = Mix 4) -- CONFIRMED 2026-08-31 via the cat-0x04 readback, which returns an independent record for each of the four indices (the original capture had only ever shown mix 0); [19]=channel **0-32**: 1-32 = the input strips (each mix has 32 -- the user's solo click re-sent all 32, a handy channel-count probe) and **0 = the MIX MASTER strip** (CONFIRMED 2026-09-01 from captures/new/mix1-masterfaderplay.pcapng: sweeping the Mix 1 master fader emits 68 frames, all `d4 05 00 00 <fader> 20 60` -- channel 0, pan/send held constant. The Launcher writes channel 0 itself, so it is a normal target); [20]=FADER, raw = attenuation in -dB, 0 = 0dB/unity .. 90 = -90dB (matches the UI's 0..-90 range); [21]=PAN + FLAGS -- low 6 bits (pan_mask) = pan, pan_center 0x20, so 0x02 = full-left (-30), 0x20 = center, 0x3e = full-right (+30) i.e. raw = 32 + degrees; bit 0x40 = MUTE; bit 0x80 = SOLO; [22]=SEND level, 0-96 (0x60 = 0dB, 0 = -inf; same 0-96 scale as bus_level). No target byte past 22. READBACK: frame.readback category 0x04, index = mix number 0..3 -- FULLY DECODED + hardware round-trip verified 2026-08-31. The record is 33 three-byte slots in this frame's own field order (fader, pan|flags, send); slot N is exactly the strip written as `channel` N -- including slot 0 = channel 0 = the mix master -- so the readback and the write frame share a layout the way routing does, with no special case at either end. That round trip also confirmed [18] really is the mix number (all four mixes return their own record) and that [22] is stored send state, not a meter. protocol.parse_mixer_record; CLI `mix-status`. Also category 0x1b = the SURROUND GLOBAL readback, not a mixer table (corrected 2026-09-04 -- see frame.readback.categories.0x1b); mixer BUS levels are in the 0x73 state report's bus_block (offsets 28-45), not in any readback category. CLI: `mix-set <mix> <ch|master> [--fader dB] [--pan] [--send] [--mute] [--solo]`, which read-modify-writes the strip via the cat-0x04 readback (this frame carries the WHOLE strip, so a partial write would reset the untouched fields) and verifies afterwards. Direct builder: build_mix_command(profile, mix, channel, fader, pan_deg, send, mute, solo).

auraverb_command.notes: Its own command shape (opcode 0x1d) -- the AuraVerb reverb on the Mix 1 window (a device-BUNDLED Synergy Core effect: always present, no per-plugin activation -- IN SCOPE, unlike the licensed AFX plugin chain). DSP PARAMS DECODED from macos-auraverb-ctl-color-predelay-earlyrefgaij-laterefdelay-richness-reverbtime-roomsize-reverblevel (2026-08-31, native macOS): the user swept each of the 8 AuraVerb controls one at a time. Frame offsets 16-28: [16]=0xda param_id; [17]=0x0b constant sub-cmd; [18]=0x00 constant (only Mix 1 captured -- likely the mix index, AuraVerb lives on a mix window); [19]=Room Size; [20]=Color; [21]=Pre-Delay (0-100 maps to 0-32 ms per the public manual); [22]=0x64 (100) constant, NEVER swept -- assumed the wet/mix amount locked at 100% (AuraVerb runs 100% wet as a mix send), could also be a 9th unexposed control; [23]=Early Reflection Gain; [24]=Late Reflection Delay; [25]=Richness; [26]=Reverb Time; [27]=Reverb Level; [28]=enabled (01 on / 00 off, from macos-auraverb-on-off). Every param is a plain 0-100 byte (UI drags land on even values, granularity 2, but odd values are presumably legal); Color reached exactly 0x64=100, the rest topped out at 0x62=98 only because the drag stopped short. The frame carries ALL 8 params + enabled every time (whole-state, like the mixer). Control names + ranges cross-checked against the Orion Studio Synergy Core user manual p.50 and antelopeaudio.com/products/auraverb (facts only). No 0x73 readback -- BUT there IS a dedicated readback: frame.readback category 0x0a (decoded + hardware-confirmed 2026-09-03, see readback.categories.0x0a and protocol.parse_auraverb_record). CLI `auraverb` now live-reads that and does a verified read-modify-write; the old CLI cache is kept only as an offline fallback. defaults[] = the device power-on values seen frozen in macos-auraverb-on-off. build_auraverb_command + CLI `auraverb`; 0x1d in constraints.allowed_opcodes (2026-08-31). The [22]=0x64 wet/mix constant is mirrored in the 0x0a readback and stayed 100 through the whole differential sweep -- consistent with a fixed 100%-wet lock, not a hidden 9th control.

micmodeling_command.channel_bias_note: byte 18 = 0-based input channel index + channel_bias, i.e. preamp 5 (index 4) -> 0, preamp 7 (index 6) -> 2, preamp 12 (index 11) -> 7
micmodeling_command.channels_note: 0-based input channel indices with mic modeling -- preamps 5-12 (8 channels = the 8 emumic routing taps, bank 0x01 idx 0-7). The front-panel/Launcher EMU button shows on a channel only in Mic mode (absent in Line/Hi-Z) -- earlier work saw '7-12' because the reference unit had preamps 5-6 in Line. FULLY CONFIRMED 2026-09-03 by a live usbmon capture of the webUI driving EMU on preamp 5/6 (captures/new/webui-emumic-preamp56-2026-09-03.frames.txt): the 0xe5 frame carries [18]=0x00 for preamp 5 and [18]=0x01 for preamp 6 -- the channel_bias -4 mapping holds to the bottom of the range, directly observed on the wire (was extrapolation). The pair is link pair 2 (SET_LINK 0x14 a2 00 02 seen on disable), and the phantom/gain sync commands (SET_PARAM 0x51 / 0x50) address the pair as channel index 4 & 5.
micmodeling_command.pattern_range_note: [0,100] is the model-0 (EdgeDuo raw) continuous morph range. For a selected emulation model [22] is a small index whose max is model-dependent: 0 (fixed), 2 (3-way), or 8 (9-detent multipattern). See notes and mic_models.json.
micmodeling_command.notes: MIC MODELING / 'emuMic' -- the front-panel EMU button on preamps 5-12 (8 channels), shown per channel only in Mic mode. Runs Antelope's mic-emulation DSP (for their Edge Solo / Edge Duo / Edge Note modelling mics + model packs). Opcode 0x17 is SHARED: param_id at [16] disambiguates -- 0xd4 = virtual mixer (frame.mix_command), 0xe5 = mic modeling. Frame `e5 05 <ch> <en> <model> <swap> <pattern>`, bytes 16-22, rest 0. [17]=0x05 const; [18]=channel = 0-based input channel index - 4 (preamp 7 -> 2 ... preamp 12 -> 7); [19]=modeling ENABLED (1/0); [20]=MODEL ID (0 = EdgeDuo / raw mic, no emulation -- the default; 1..N = the emulation models, see profiles/mic_models.json); [21]=CHANNEL-ORDER SWAP (0/1); [22]=POLAR PATTERN, always a 0-based INDEX (NOT a class code -- corrected 2026-09-01 from macos-emumic-polar-patterns). With model 0 (EdgeDuo raw) it is the free 0-100 continuous morph (0 omni / 50 cardioid / 100 figure-8), user-confirmed. With an emulation model selected it is a small integer index into that model's pattern list, and its range is per-model: fixed mics lock it at 0 (models 2,5,6,8,13,14,15,17 -- one pattern); models 3,4,7 sweep 0..2 (omni/cardioid/fig-8); models 9,10,11 sweep 0..8 (9-detent multipattern); models 1,12,16,18 only 0..1 were swept (a 3rd value may exist -- not confirmed). Selecting a model writes [22] = that model's DEFAULT pattern index (0 for fixed, 1 = cardioid for the 3-way mics, 4 = cardioid for the 9-way mics) -- this is the value earlier misrecorded as 'pattern_class' in mic_models.json. Enable/pattern(model 0)/swap decoded 2026-08-31 from macos-ch7-8-micmodeling-* / macos-ch9-10_11-12-micmodeling-*; model IDs from 'emumic-model-select-...' (Windows KVM, 18 models cycled on preamps 7-8); per-model pattern-index ranges from macos-emumic-polar-patterns (2026-09-01, all 19 models swept on preamps 7-8). Whole state every frame; params MIRROR across the linked preamp pair (Launcher sends [18]=N then [18]=N+1). Disabling sets [19]=[21]=[22]=0. SIDE EFFECTS of enabling: the Launcher also turns on 48V phantom for the pair (SET_PARAM param 0x51) and links the preamp pair (SET_LINK space 0). No readback CATEGORY identified in the 0x74/0x75 protocol (cat 0x1a turned out to be the surround per-speaker EQ, cat 0x07 is unresolved EQ/filter data -- neither is mic modeling); in the passive 0x73 stream only the phantom bit (0x10) moves. build_micmodeling_command(profile, channel, enabled, pattern, swap, model); not in cli.py.

Bucket C (read 'which channel holds which plugin instance') is documented here; bucket B (per-slot bypass) is documented but ships NO builder; the write that places/clears a plugin (opcode 0x23) stays in constraints.forbidden_opcodes = bucket E, OFF-LIMITS. assign.opcode_note: 0x23 is in constraints.forbidden_opcodes; build_* refuses it. Placing or clearing a plugin on a channel insert = bucket E (instantiate/load/remove), OFF-LIMITS per SCOPE.md. Documented here for observation + future readback decoding, not to emit.
assign.handle_note: plugin-instance HANDLE. Observed 0x48 (Tuner), 0x49 (MemoryCat Brigade); 0x00 = clear this channel's insert. The same handle keys the bypass frame ([18]) and the parameter frame (0x1c/0xd5 [18]). Plausibly 0x40 | slot_index (-> AFX slots 8, 9) or a sequential instance id -- only 2 data points. The handles pre-existed at capture start (plugins loaded in a prior Launcher session); this frame moves an existing instance onto/off a channel, it was never seen to create one.

bypass.value_note: 0/1 toggle driven by the plugin's bypass control. Polarity not certain -- in the MemoryCat capture value=1 was held throughout parameter editing, suggesting 1 = ACTIVE / 0 = BYPASSED. Bucket B (a mixer-level insert mute, cf. AuraVerb enabled@28): exposing it is permitted, but a builder needs a handle from the readback (not decoded), so none ships.

afx_slot.readback: On each slot change the Launcher re-reads readback categories 0x0c AND 0x15 (index 0) -- the '90-entry <id><flags>' tables -- so those are very likely the AFX slot-occupancy / plugin map (bucket C). Partial only: in the 0x0c response, bytes [7] and [19] step 0x30->0x32 when one plugin is placed, and one entry in a trailing run of 0x60 (=96) goes 0x60->0x00. Full decode deferred to ../antelope-ctl-afx (Phase 1).
afx_slot.notes: AFX plugin-chain SLOT control -- NOT plugin parameters. SCOPE.md buckets: read 'channel N holds plugin X / bypassed' = C (here); per-slot bypass = B (here, builder gated on the readback); place/remove a plugin = E (0x23 forbidden); plugin parameters (0x1c/0xd5) and activation traffic = F, never in this repo. AuraVerb (0x1d, frame.auraverb_command) is the only plugin fully in scope here, and only because it is device-bundled with no activation.

state_report.channel_meter_scale: inverted: 0x60 (96) at rest/silence, falls toward 0x00 as level rises. Same scale as meter_report.db_curve (raw ~= -dBFS), reuse that curve.
state_report.channel_meter_notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-05, full writeup + byte-level evidence in the antelope-ctl-UI-test sandbox's webui/METERS.md (webui/ isn't in this repo) -- this is NOT a fixed per-channel analog-input tap, and NOT a fixed per-`surround_in`-channel tap either (an earlier pass at this note claimed the latter; disproven by a follow-up test). DECISIVE TEST: with a live mic signal on preamp 2 already showing at byte 158 (via surround_in ch2, which preamp 2 was routed into), routing that SAME preamp-2 signal into a SECOND destination (mix_ch1 routing-dest strip 1, dest id 10, channel 0) made byte **157** light up to match it too -- even though surround_in ch1 had nothing routed into it and stayed untouched throughout. So 157 is not 'surround_in channel 1' specifically: it is a slot in a small SHARED POOL that gets dynamically claimed by whichever internal signal path(s) currently carry audio, drawn from across multiple distinct buses (surround_in, mix_ch strips, and probably others untested) -- not a fixed identity per byte. It shows correct preamp levels only when surround_in happens to be routed straight-through from the matching preamp AND nothing else in the pool's scope is competing for that slot -- both true by default, which is why this looked like a clean per-preamp meter for so long. The exact allocation rule (which bus(es) feed the pool, order/priority when multiple signals compete for the same slot count) is UNRESOLVED -- every test so far has had at most 2 simultaneous active signals; a live-capture-based investigation (see PROTOCOL.md methodology) is more likely to resolve this than further black-box polling, which already produced several since-retracted false leads during this same investigation (see the sandbox's webui/METERS.md). Three identical mirror copies of the whole 12-byte pool still exist at bases 157, 169 and 221 -- use 157. This supersedes meter_report.channel_meter_base_offset (0x75 @32), which on this unit is NOT per-channel: only its byte 32 is live (a monitor/summed level) and byte 33 is a 0/1 flag that the old 32+channel formula misreads as channel 1 pinned at clip.
state_report.notes: Parallel-array layout: all channel gains contiguous from gain_base_offset, all status bytes contiguous from status_base_offset. Formula: status_byte = (phase<<6)|(phantom<<4)|(mode&0x03).

bus_block.notes: Same 'parallel array, N bytes per slot' idea as gain_base_offset/status_base_offset above, but for output buses instead of input channels: byte offset for bus N = base_offset + bytes_per_bus*N + field_offset. Confirmed for ALL 6 bus ids: 0/1/2/5 via captures mona/hp1/hp2/monb (2026-08, level ramps + dim/mute/mono toggles), and 3/4 (line/reamp) via capture settings-linevol-mute-reampvol-toggle (2026-08, level ramps at offsets 37 and 40 + a mute toggle on bus 3). Every SET_PARAM command in each log matched the very next state_report reading at this formula's offset. reserved_byte_offset (+2) never changed in any capture; true padding, or just never exercised, is unconfirmed. dim/mono were never exercised on buses 3/4 and may not apply to a line/reamp output. NOTE: the status byte's mute bit (0x04) also reads 1 whenever that bus is at level 96 with no mute command -- see params.bus_mute.

target_0.notes: 3-bit field, value<<4 at offset 24. capture settings-trim-mona-monb-line-panlaw (2026-08): SET_PARAM(0x4b, target=0, value 0..6) -> offset 24 stepped 0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30/0x40/0x50/0x60, i.e. exactly value<<4, every step. Almost certainly the Monitor A output trim (first target swept, capture name order mona/monb/line).

target_1.notes: 3-bit field, value<<2 at offset 25 bits 2-4. Same capture: SET_PARAM(0x4b, target=1, value 0..6) -> 0x00/0x04/0x08/0x0c/0x10/0x14/0x18. Almost certainly Monitor B output trim.

target_2.notes: 3-bit field, value<<5 at offset 25 bits 5-7. Same capture: SET_PARAM(0x4b, target=2, value 0..6) -> 0x00/0x20/0x40/0x60/0x80/0xa0/0xc0. Almost certainly Line output trim.

output_trim_block.notes: A small packed block just before bus_block, holding the settings-tab output-trim selectors (param 0x4b). Three targets (0/1/2 = Monitor A / Monitor B / Line Out) confirmed, each a 7-position 1-dBu-per-step selector (0 = 20 dBu .. 6 = 14 dBu, see params.output_trim.trim_dbu); readback is value<<shift. RE-CONFIRMED live on the device 2026-09-03 (swept all 3, restored). UNUSED bits: offset 24 bits 0-3 and 7, offset 25 bits 0-1. Pan law is NOT here and NOT a 4th target of 0x4b -- tested live 2026-09-03 (SET_PARAM 0x4b target 3 values 0..3 had zero effect anywhere); it needs its own Launcher capture. Readback cat 0x16 (once guessed to hold trim/pan-law) does NOT track either -- ruled out the same day.

sample_rate_byte_offset.notes: The device sample-rate INDEX (0-6, see params.sample_rate.values), one plain byte. CONFIRMED from capture macos-smplrt-32k-44k1-48-88k2-96k-176k4-192k (2026-08, native macOS): the user stepped 32k/44k1/48k/88k2/96k/176k4/192k; each SET_GLOBAL(param 0x03, value V) was followed ~1 s later (device clock re-lock settle) by offset 18 == V, monotonic 0..6. This overlaps the old 'offset 17/19 blip' region -- offset 18 itself is the sample rate, NOT blip noise; offset 19 = clock source (see clock_source_byte_offset), offset 17 is still the ~3 s Launcher-handshake blip. Offsets 21/22/23/27 also move with the rate -- DECODED 2026-09-04, see clock_rate_hz_offset. See params.sample_rate.

clock_rate_hz_offset.notes: DECODED 2026-09-04 by a live hardware sweep (clock=OVEN, every rate stepped, 0x73 read at each). Offsets [21][22][23] = the actual running sample rate in Hz as a 24-bit BIG-ENDIAN integer ([21]<<16 | [22]<<8 | [23]): 44100=00ac44, 48000=00bb80, 88200=015888, 96000=017700, 176400=02b110, 192000=02ee00. (32k untested this pass -- expect 007d00.) Offset [27] = rate-family one-hot, = 0x10 >> [21]: 0x10 base family (<=48k), 0x08 double (88.2/96k), 0x04 quad (176.4/192k). Read under the internal (OVEN) clock, so [21-23] echoed the commanded rate; whether under an external clock it reports the MEASURED incoming rate (making it a genuine lock/rate monitor) is not yet tested. Complements offset 18 (the 0-6 enum): this is the frequency in Hz. protocol.state_clock_rate_hz(profile, data).

clock_source_byte_offset.notes: The device clock source index (0-6, see params.clock_source.values), one plain byte. CONFIRMED from capture clock-source-WC-adat-adatx2-adatx4-spdif-usb-oven (2026-09-03, usbmon): SET_GLOBAL(param 0x04, value V) and offset 19 tracked 1:1 through all seven options. This resolves the old unresolved_state_offsets entry for offset 19 -- the '0x06 -> 0x00 ~3 s after connect' blip is the clock re-locking from USB (6) to the device's saved source at startup, not handshake noise. See params.clock_source.

screen_brightness_byte_offset.notes: The device's front-panel screen brightness, 0-100 (0x00-0x64), one plain byte. CONFIRMED from capture macos-scrbrght-0-100-50-multvalue (2026-08, native macOS -- the user watched the physical screen dim/brighten in real time): every SET_PARAM(opcode 0x12, param 0x0e, value V) was followed by offset 26 == V in the very next 0x73 report, 25/25 commands, values 0x00..0x64. So screen brightness IS a real, persisted, readable device setting (NOT host-side -- the earlier settings-scrbrght-surroundEQ capture under the VM simply never reached the device / the slider did nothing under the VM). Sits in the previously-unmapped gap between output_trim_block (24-25) and bus_block (28-45). Offset 27 still unmapped. See params.screen_brightness.

source_low.notes: LOW 2 BITS of the talkback source index only. Confirmed from capture talkback-select (2026-08): selecting sources 0..12 in turn, offset 73 bits 0-1 always equalled source_index & 0x03 (13/13 samples). The high bits of the source index are NOT exposed anywhere found in the 0x73 report -- offsets 72 and 75 stayed 0x00 for the whole sweep. So you can read talkback source back only mod 4 from the device; track the full value client-side.

dest_assign.notes: 4-bit bitmask, one bit per talkback destination (Mon A / Mon B / HP1 / HP2): destination N assigned = bit (N+2), i.e. dest0=0x04, dest1=0x08, dest2=0x10, dest3=0x20. Confirmed from capture talkback-bttn (2026-08): toggling each of the 4 switches in isolation set/cleared exactly its bit. Multi-destination combining is USER-CONFIRMED (2026-08) -- talkback can be sent to all 4 at once, so this byte can legitimately hold several of these bits set together.

button.notes: Talkback button / hold-to-talk active. Confirmed from capture talkback-bttn (2026-08): press -> bit 6 set, release -> cleared, every time.

talkback_block.notes: Sits immediately after the 12-byte channel status array (status_base_offset 61 + 12 = 73). offset 73 is a packed talkback status byte (see status_bits); offset 74 is the talkback gain (0-96, same scale as bus_level, 96=0dB) of the CURRENTLY SELECTED source -- confirmed from talkback-gain-int-ch1-2-12 (2026-08): sweeping param 0x20 moved offset 74 1:1 across 0-96, and re-selecting the source reset offset 74 to that source's own stored gain (so talkback gain is per-source, but only the selected source's value is visible here). CAVEAT: source_low and dest_assign share bits 2-3 (source index 4-12 sets bits that also mean dest0/dest1 assigned). The talkback-select and talkback-bttn captures were separate sessions -- source was 0 during the dest toggles and no dest/button was set during the source sweep -- so how these coexist in one byte when both are non-default is UNTESTED. Needs a combined capture before trusting the readback with talkback fully configured.

meter_report.channel_meter_scale: inverted: 0x60 (96) at rest/silence, falls toward 0x00 as level rises
meter_report.notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-01: on this unit the 0x75 frame is NOT a per-channel meter. Only byte 32 is live -- a monitor/summed level that moves for any input -- and byte 33 is a 0/1 flag. The old '32 + channel, confirmed for all 12' claim was wrong: a dedicated recapture feeding preamps 1-4 in turn showed no movement past byte 32, and the byte-33 flag was rendered as channel 1 stuck at clip. The real metering (a shared dynamic pool of active-signal slots, not a fixed per-channel or per-bus tap -- see the 2026-09-05 correction on state_report.channel_meter_notes) is in the 0x73 state report -- see state_report.channel_meter_base_offset (157 + channel). db_curve below (raw ~= -dBFS) still applies to those. Kept here for the offset-32 monitor reading and the shared curve.
meter_report.db_curve_notes: Channel 0 only, 1kHz sine, gain swept down from max while phase_invert was clicked as a timestamp marker at each reference point (a real command, so it shows up as an unambiguous status-byte bit flip -- a cheap way to bookmark a capture without a second command-frame log). Raw byte == -dB, essentially exactly, across the whole 0 to -60dB range swept (the -60 point originally logged as raw=59, not 60, but that was the user eyeballing a color bar rather than a number while manually dragging the gain slider -- not curve non-linearity, corrected to 60). Not yet swept: the red/orange LED boundary, and anything past -60dB (one stray, unexplained data point -- raw=72 at gain driven to 0/deep silence -- doesn't fit this line at all, but wasn't a deliberate reference point, see notes above). Not yet confirmed on other channels, but likely identical given the same offset formula holds for all 12.

led_scale.notes: Confirmed 2026-08: no separate solid-red band below clip -- orange runs all the way to 0dB, red only appears at clip.

init_enumeration_report.record_layout: header 0x74, u32 constant 0x10 @4, u32 category_id @8, u32 index @12 (0-based, 0..count-1 within a category); nothing non-zero past offset 16. Records carry (category_id, index) ONLY -- no names (names would be USB string descriptors, i.e. control transfers, not in the 320-byte HID capture).
init_enumeration_report.notes: This burst IS the readback protocol (frame.readback) -- the Launcher walking every (category, index). Decoded 2026-08-31: the host SENDS a 0x74 request `74 00 00 00 10 00 00 00 <cat> 00 00 00 <idx> 00 00 00` on EP 0x01 OUT and the device REPLIES with `75 00 00 00 40 01 00 00 <cat> ... <idx> ... <data>` on EP 0x82 IN. It is not names-only and not one-shot -- it carries live state (routing = cat 0x03, mixer = cat 0x04, AuraVerb = cat 0x0a, ...). The text below is the original (pre-decode) analysis of the connect burst, kept for the emission-order detail. A one-shot device topology enumeration. Seen ONLY in all_reports_AntelopeINIT.tsv (113 records, t=7.5-16s of the connect sequence), never in any other capture. That capture is the Antelope Launcher being launched with NO user interaction (confirmed by the user) -- so this whole burst, and the single outgoing 0x70/SET_PARAM(param 0x49) at t=7.71s, is the Launcher's automatic startup/handshake, not anything a user did. Full emission order (see PROTOCOL.md section 4): 0x11 x2 (S/PDIF); 0x0b marker; 0x1b x1 singleton; 0x1a x16 (SURROUND PER-SPEAKER EQ, one per speaker -- NOT ADAT; see frame.readback.categories.0x1a, live-read 2026-09-04. The old 'ADAT' label was a 16==16 count guess; ADAT has no readback category); 0x03 x15 (unmapped); 0x04 x4 (unmapped, each entry trailed by its own 0x0b=3 marker); 0x0a x1, 0x15 x1, 0x16 x1 singletons; 0x19 x64 (unmapped -- almost certainly the 64-channel USB/Thunderbolt stream, the device's headline I/O count; routing command's first payload byte 0x41=65 is consistent with a 1-based index into a 64-entry space); 0x0b closing markers. 0x0b (8 records, index values 1/2/3/3/3/3/0/4) is a section/phase marker, NOT an I/O category. Confirmed: 0x1a=ADAT, 0x11=S/PDIF. Still unnamed: 0x19/0x03/0x04 and the four singletons. NOTE (2026-08): checked all 21 raw pcapng files -- NOT ONE contains a USB string-descriptor fetch, and the UAC2 descriptor is a stub with no channel names. So the names are Launcher-internal and cannot be recovered from any capture on file; the practical routes are (a) a fresh connect capture where Windows re-fetches string descriptors, or (b) reading the counts off against the Launcher's routing-tab labels. This is NOT a live settings readback -- indices only, no current values. Listed here mainly so scan tools stop flagging 0x74 as unknown. CROSS-PLATFORM CONFIRMED (2026-08): the four native-macOS INIT captures (macos-antelopeINIT-*) reproduce this exactly -- same 0x74 burst (byte-identical between captures with different device state), and the SAME single outgoing handshake frame SET_PARAM(param 0x49, channel 1, value 0). That one 0x49 frame is the ENTIRE host->device connect handshake; everything else the Launcher does at connect is either passive polling or cosmetic state restore (a SET_PARAM(gain 0x50) fade-in ramp). macOS capture layout: 40-byte Darwin pseudo-header + 320-byte payload (frame.len==360), payload byte 0 = magic; 0x74 arrives on IN endpoint 1, 0x73/0x75 on IN endpoint 2.

readback.status: DECODED 2026-08-31 (CAPTURE E' -- usbmon on the Linux host while the Windows Launcher connected over QEMU USB passthrough -- then replayed directly from Linux, tools/readback_enum.py). This is the device-side readback the earlier analysis had concluded did not exist. It is an in-band request/response on the SAME HID interrupt endpoints, NOT a HID Feature report and NOT a control transfer -- which is why tools/hid_probe.py (no Feature report, GET_REPORT STALLs) and tools/readback_probe.py did not find it.
readback.request: host->device, EP 0x01 OUT, full 320-byte report: 74 00 00 00 | 10 00 00 00 | <category> 00 00 00 | <index> 00 00 00 | 00...  (magic 0x74 @0, subcmd 0x10 @4, category @8, index @12)
readback.response: device->host, EP 0x82 IN, full 320-byte report: 75 00 00 00 | 40 01 00 00 | <category> 00 00 00 | <index> 00 00 00 | <data...>  (magic 0x75 @0, discriminator 0x00 @1, category @8, index @12, payload from @16)
readback.discriminator_note: The response magic is 0x75 but byte 1 = 0x00. The free-running METER report is also magic 0x75 but byte 1 = 0x1f; the STATE report (frame.state_report) is the same family with magic 0x73 -- effectively 'category 0, pushed continuously'. So (magic 0x75 AND byte1 0x00 AND category AND index) uniquely identifies a readback response amid the ~250 Hz state/meter stream.
readback.liveness: The device answers EVERY (category, index) that is IN RANGE -- one it has no record for just comes back with an empty body. 'has a non-empty body' is the real liveness signal. Scalar categories return the same record for every index. Pace queries and reopen on halt (tools/readback_enum.py, transport.HidTransport.query).
readback.namespace_warning: READBACK CATEGORY NUMBERS AND COMMAND OPCODE NUMBERS ARE TWO SEPARATE NAMESPACES THAT OVERLAP. The same byte value means different things depending on where it sits: at frame offset 4 it is a command OPCODE, at the readback request's category_offset it is a CATEGORY. Colliding values in use here: 0x12 (opcode SET_GLOBAL / category UNKNOWN-empty), 0x13 (opcode SET_PARAM / category unqueried), 0x14 (opcode SET_LINK / category unqueried), 0x17 (opcode SET_MIX+SET_MIC_MODELING / category unqueried), 0x1a (opcode BLOCKED as an unconfirmed precaution -- never actually observed as a write opcode on this device, see constraints.forbidden_opcodes_note / category SURROUND PER-SPEAKER EQ, decoded + in scope), 0x1b (category SURROUND GLOBAL, decoded + in scope), 0x1c (opcode FORBIDDEN, AFX licensed-plugin PARAMETER stream -- bucket D / category answers empty), 0x1d (opcode SET_AURAVERB, bundled + no activation, in scope / category answers empty), 0x23 (opcode AFX slot-assign, FORBIDDEN -- bucket E, places/clears a licensed plugin / category answers empty). This has already caused one documented misread: category 0x1a was labelled 'ADAT' for weeks purely because its record count (16) matched the ADAT channel count, and the surround-EQ content was never checked (corrected 2026-09-04). A second, related misread to avoid: 'forbidden opcode' here is a SCOPE.md policy about Antelope's purchasable, activation-gated AFX/Cosmos plugin catalogue, not a stance against the device's built-in DSP -- AuraVerb (0x1d) and the surround per-speaker EQ (readback category 0x1a) both run on the same DSP unit and are fully decoded and in scope. When reading these docs, always check which namespace a hex value is in.
readback.hazard: DO NOT QUERY AN INDEX PAST A CATEGORY'S RECORD COUNT. The firmware does not bounds-check the index: one index past the end returns adjacent memory with a WRONG layout, and a little further it faults. Confirmed 2026-08-31 on real hardware -- `category 0x04 index 5` hard-crashed the Orion Studio III (front panel: 'CRITICAL ERROR! / Failure.c / L: 204  E: 0 / BusFault_Handler' -- a Cortex-M BusFault) and the unit needed a physical power cycle. Diagnostic signature, in order: cat 0x04 idx 0-3 = four same-layout mixer records; idx 4 = answers but with a completely different layout (a float32 table = adjacent memory); idx 5 = NO response at all, then the OUT endpoint is dead. An EMPTY answer is normal; NO answer means the MCU just died inside the handler. NOTE: this supersedes the earlier diagnosis that the endpoint halt was caused by 'hammering' / query rate -- the 2026-08-31 crash took about ten slow queries. Rate was never the trigger; the out-of-range index was. Enforced by protocol.check_readback_index against readback.category_counts.

identity._comment: LAYOUT ONLY -- the serial VALUE is never stored in this repo. It is read from the hardware on request (CLI `identity --serial`). Same record shape on the Orion Studio III and the Zen Go Synergy Core, so it is probably family-wide.
identity.notes: Category 0x01 is a 48-byte record of NUL-terminated ASCII at fixed offsets: model name @0, SERIAL @20 (13 chars), hardware revision @36, then 4 binary bytes @44 (little-endian u32; both units seen decode to mid-2021, so plausibly a build/calibration timestamp -- a GUESS, not confirmed). Category 0x00 is a separate record: 12 bytes with an ASCII firmware version at offset 8 (e.g. '4.41'). Parsed by protocol.parse_identity_record / parse_firmware_record.

readback.category_counts_note: Record counts taken from the device's OWN 0x74 connect enumeration (frame.init_enumeration_report -- 113 records = 16+2+64+15+4+4+8, so these ten categories are the whole walk). This is the only evidence-grade count we have and it is the safe query bound (see .hazard). Categories that answer but do NOT appear in the connect walk (0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x05, 0x06, 0x07, 0x0c, 0x0d, 0x12) have NO known count -- protocol.build_readback_query cannot bound them, so treat any index above 0 on those as unproven and dangerous. Note that cat 0x03 answers with distinct bodies at idx 15-24 even though it only has 15 destination groups: that is already adjacent memory, not extra routing data. `0x1a` = 16 is the SURROUND PER-SPEAKER EQ (16 speakers), not ADAT -- see categories.0x1a; the count is right either way (16), but the label was a guess.

categories.0x01: model name ('OrionStudio_III') + serial + hw rev ('7.0') -- CONTAINS THE DEVICE SERIAL, do not commit raw dumps
categories.0x03: ROUTING MATRIX -- one record per destination group, index = dest_id 0..14. Record = <dest_id> then a (source_bank, source_index) pair per output channel of that group (destination_channels[dest_id] pairs), identical layout to the frame.routing_command write frame. VERIFIED byte-identical against CLI-written routes 2026-08-31.
categories.0x04: VIRTUAL MIXER -- one record per mix, index = mix number 0..3 (= Mix 1..4). Record = a flat array of 33 three-byte slots, SAME field order as the frame.mix_command write frame: <fader> <pan|mute|solo> <send>. Slot index maps 1:1 onto frame.mix_command's `channel` field with NO special case: slot 0 = the MIX MASTER strip, slots 1..32 = the 32 input strips. 99 bytes on the wire, zero-padded to the report size. DECODED + HARDWARE-CONFIRMED, both halves. (a) INPUTS, 2026-08-31: wrote mix 1 / ch 5 / fader 40 / pan +12 / mute / send 33 (frame bytes `28 6c 21`), read the record back and slot 5 was `28 6c 21` with NO other slot changed; three reads 2.5s apart -- and later 142 reads over 150s -- were byte-identical, so the third byte is stored send state and not a live meter. (b) MASTER, 2026-09-01: a usbmon capture of the Launcher sweeping the Mix 1 master fader (captures/new/mix1-masterfaderplay.pcapng) is 68 frames, every one `d4 05 00 00 <fader> 20 60` -- mix 0, CHANNEL 0, pan and send constant; the sweep ended at fader 90 and slot 0 then read back as -90 dB. The Launcher itself addresses channel 0, so it is a normal target and NOT an out-of-range write. protocol.parse_mixer_record; CLI `mix-status`. This is the mixer readback that frame.mix_command's notes used to say did not exist -- it is not in the 0x73 state report, it is here.
categories.0x05: PREAMP GAIN -- one plain byte per physical input channel = gain in dB (line/direct read 0). Independent copy of the 0x73 state report's gain array (state_report.gain_base_offset 49). DECODED + differential-write confirmed 2026-09-03 (`set-gain 7 33` -> byte [7] = 0x21, nothing else moved). protocol.parse_preamp_gain_record; selftest cross-checks it against 0x73.
categories.0x06: CHANNEL STATUS -- one byte per physical input channel, SAME packing as the 0x73 state report status array (state_report.status_base_offset 61 / status_bits): (phase_invert<<6)|(phantom<<4)|(mode&0x03). DECODED + differential-write confirmed 2026-09-03 (`set-invert 7 on` -> byte [7]=0x40; `set-mode 7 line` -> 0x41; phantom bit 0x10 follows the same shared encoding, not re-exercised -- no +48V on the reference unit during the sweep). protocol.parse_channel_status_record.
categories.0x07: EQ / filter band data -- same `<freq LE16><Q LE16 x100><gain LE16 signed><mode>` stride as the surround per-speaker EQ (0x1a below, frame.surround_speaker). Records are HETEROGENEOUS (live-read 2026-09-04): idx 0 and idx 1 are 8 x a flat 5-band EQ (30/200/1k/5k/15k Hz, Q 0.71, gain 0, modes 0/2/2/2/1); idx 2 is 16 x a 19-byte record `01 <e803=1000> 0000 <2710=10000> 0000 ffff <64=100> 00000000 <18=24> 00` that looks like a per-band RANGE/capability descriptor, not live state. Purpose unresolved -- possibly a monitor/phones EQ or a capability table for the surround EQ. NOT a per-input-channel EQ (the Synergy Core has none -- input EQ is an AFX plugin). Not in the 0x74 connect walk, so no safe index bound above 0.
categories.0x0a: AuraVerb parameters -- DECODED + HARDWARE-CONFIRMED 2026-09-03 (protocol.parse_auraverb_record). Single record (index 0). Layout: a 0x00 header byte, then four 11-byte blocks (Mix 1..4); the 43-byte record truncates block 4 to 9 bytes. Each block = the frame.auraverb_command payload minus its [18] mix byte: [0]room_size [1]color [2]pre_delay [3]0x64(wet const) [4]early_reflection_gain [5]late_reflection_delay [6]richness [7]reverb_time [8]reverb_level [9]enabled(01/00) [10]0xff(const). Decoded by differential readback -- set one param via `auraverb --<flag>`, re-read, see which byte moved; every param + the enable bit pinned this way and writing the pre-sweep values back reproduced the record byte-for-byte. CLI `auraverb` now live-reads this and does a verified read-modify-write; selftest.py t_auraverb / t_write_auraverb.
categories.0x0b: in the 0x74 CONNECT WALK it is a section/phase marker (8 records, index values 1/2/3/3/3/3/0/4), NOT an I/O category -- see frame.init_enumeration_report. A direct query at idx 0 answered with a scalar 0x01 in 2026-08 and with an EMPTY body on 2026-09-04, so treat it as structural, not state.
categories.0x0d: scalar 0x18 (=24). Re-read 2026-09-04, same value. Meaning unknown; stable across reads so it is a constant or a slowly-changing capability, not live state. Not in the 0x74 connect walk (no safe index bound above 0).
categories.0x11: S/PDIF + a capability bitmask block (128 bytes)
categories.0x12: UNKNOWN. A 2026-08 probe saw a scalar; a direct query at idx 0 returned an EMPTY body on 2026-09-04. The old 'clock source or sample-rate index?' guess is RULED OUT -- both of those read back from the 0x73 state report instead (clock source @19, sample-rate index @18, rate in Hz @21-23), confirmed on hardware 2026-09-03/04. Not in the 0x74 connect walk, so no safe index bound above 0. NB: readback category 0x12 is NOT the same thing as command opcode 0x12 (SET_GLOBAL) -- see frame.readback.namespace_warning.
categories.0x16: UNKNOWN, ~8-16 bytes. NOT output trim and NOT pan law -- both ruled out 2026-09-03 by a live differential test: sweeping SET_PARAM 0x4b targets 0/1/2 (the confirmed output-trim targets) moved 0x73 [24]/[25] exactly as documented but left 0x16 untouched, and SET_PARAM 0x4b target 3 (the pan-law hypothesis) did nothing anywhere. Content seen: all-zero (2026-09-03), '00 00 00 32 00 00 00 32 01 12 00 01 01 12 00 01' (2026-09-01) -- so it does carry state sometimes; source unidentified (possibly transient / a webUI-touched value). Still undecoded.
categories.0x1a: SURROUND PER-SPEAKER EQ readback -- the readback for the launcher-only 0x87/0xea frame (params.surround_speaker). 116 bytes = 4-byte header (`00 00 58 02`) + 16 EQ bands x 7 bytes, EXACT same layout as the write frame: `<freq LE16 Hz><Q LE16 x100><gain LE16 signed 0.01 dB><mode 0/1/2>`. One record per surround speaker, index 0..15 (this is what the 0x74 connect walk's `0x1a x16` actually is -- NOT ADAT; ADAT was a 16==16 count guess and has NO readback category, its gain/link is in 0x73 @75-90). LIVE-READ 2026-09-04: idx 0 == idx 1 both carried a non-flat low-frequency curve (bands clustered 30-600 Hz, cuts/boosts to +/-12 dB) = the room-correction curve the user had generated in 2.0 -- matches their observation that RC writes an identical curve to L and R. idx 2+ were flat default templates (Q 0.71, gain 0, the log-spaced 30 Hz..15 kHz band layout). So the surround EQ / Room Correction DOES have a readback after all. Not yet wired into a parser or the CLI.
categories.0x1b: SURROUND GLOBAL readback -- the readback for the launcher-only 0xab/0xeb frame (params.surround_monitor). 1 record (idx 0). ALIGNMENT: body[N] == the 0xab write frame's byte [18+N], established 2026-09-04 by a live read against a known surround state, six independent field matches: body[0..1]=`02 9f` = frame[18][19] FORMAT 2.0; body[2]=`06` = frame[20] global delay (the 0.6 ms floor); body[4..5]=`58 02` = frame[22-23] LEVEL 600 = 0 dB; body[7..8]=`ff ff` = frame[25-26] per-speaker BYPASS mask, all active; body[9..10] = frame[27-28] MUTE mask; body[22..24]=`23 00 00` = frame[40-42], the documented bass-management marker. The 8-byte bass-management CHANNEL BLOCKS then start at body[25] = frame[43] exactly as field_map.23_onward_bass_mgmt says, and read back sensible values (LP 320 Hz / HP 80 Hz / fader 360 / order 2 on the 3 used channels, `[80][80][600][0]` defaults after) -- so this record INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMS that byte map, which had been derived only from write captures. The earlier 'mixer bus level/range table' label was wrong: the repeating `50 00 50 00 58 02 00` that prompted it is the bass-management default channel block `[80][80][600][0]`, not bus levels. Parsed + wired 2026-09-04: protocol.parse_surround_global_record, CLI `surround-status`.
categories.0x19: 64 entries, all empty in the connect walk -- the 64-ch USB/TB stream slots
categories.note: Categories 0x1c..0x60 answer but with empty bodies (probed 2026-08-31). Full raw enumeration: tools/readback_enum.py.

readback.cli: protocol.build_readback_query (bounds-checked) / check_readback_index / readback_category_count / is_readback_response / readback_body / parse_routing_record (cat 0x03) / parse_mixer_record (cat 0x04); transport.HidTransport.query; CLI `readback <cat> [idx]` (raw), `matrix-status` (live cat-0x03 read, falls back to the cache if the device is unreachable) and `mix-status [mix]` (live cat-0x04 read).
readback.history: Before 2026-08-31 the project concluded there was NO USB readback (see params.routing.readback, PROTOCOL.md, the -poke test). That was wrong: the request just needs the 10-00-00-00 sub-header + a (category,index) -- a bare 0x74 is ignored. The cross-machine persistence the user reported was the device reporting its NVRAM routing to a fresh Launcher via exactly this, not account sync.

error_response.status: unconfirmed on Orion -- confirmed on the sibling Discrete 8 Pro
error_response.notes: On the Discrete 8 Pro (peer PR): the device replies with a 0x61 frame (status byte at offset 4) ONLY when it receives an opcode it does not recognise; a recognised opcode is answered with silence. IMPORTANT: silence means 'opcode recognised', NOT 'command took effect' -- on that device opcode 0x14 was silent and did nothing. No 0x61 frame has ever appeared in an Orion capture (only 0x70/0x73/0x75/0x74), but the Launcher never sends Orion a bad opcode, so absence is not evidence. If you ever probe a candidate opcode on Orion, watch for a 0x61 reply -- and don't read silence as success.

channels.notes: Formula (byte17=N, gain@49+N, status@61+N) confirmed for all 12 physical hybrid inputs via the CLI. Hi-Z is only offered on channels 1-4 (indices 0-3) on real hardware; hiz_channels reflects that hardware constraint (user-reported, not yet cross-checked against a capture of the Launcher graying out the option on ch5-12).

link_pairs.formula: pair_index = channel_index // 2 (0-indexed channels). pair 0 = ch1&ch2, pair 1 = ch3&ch4, pair 2 = ch5&ch6, pair 3 = ch7&ch8, pair 4 = ch9&ch10, pair 5 = ch11&ch12.
link_pairs.notes: See params.channel_link for the command that sets this. Engaging a pair was observed to force the SECOND (higher-numbered) channel's input_mode and/or gain to match the first -- see channel_link.side_effects.

adat.addressing: 0-indexed ADAT channel 0-15, written to frame.command.channel_offset for adat_gain (param 0x5b). A separate address space from the 12 physical hybrid inputs -- see params.adat_gain.
adat.readback: adat gain for channel N is state_report byte (state_report.adat_gain_base_offset 75) + N, one int8 dB byte per channel, no status byte (ADAT has gain + link only, no mode/phantom/phase).

link_pairs.formula: pair_index = adat_channel_index // 2. pair 0 = ADAT ch1&ch2, ... pair 7 = ADAT ch15&ch16.
link_pairs.notes: Confirmed on real hardware (user, 2026-08): ADAT link behaves exactly like the physical-preamp link -- while a pair is linked, changing gain on one channel moves the other with it. As with physical channels, the device firmware does NOT fan a single write out to both; a controller replicates it by sending a second SET_PARAM(adat_gain) for the partner (this CLI's set-adat-gain does that when its cache says the pair is linked). See params.adat_channel_link and the SET_LINK caveat there (the ADAT and physical SET_LINK frames are byte-identical -- both use space byte 0x00 at offset 17 -- so pair_index 0-5 is shared between the two spaces; sending SET_LINK for ADAT pair N may also affect physical pair N. S/PDIF link is distinguishable: space byte 0x01).

spdif.addressing: 0-indexed S/PDIF channel: 0 = L, 1 = R. Written to frame.command.channel_offset for spdif_gain (param 0x5c). A separate address space from physical inputs and ADAT -- almost certainly the 0x11 x2 group in init_enumeration_report.
spdif.readback: spdif gain for channel N is state_report byte (state_report.spdif_gain_base_offset 91) + N -- one int8 dB byte per channel, immediately after the 16-byte ADAT gain array (75-90). No status byte (S/PDIF, like ADAT, has gain + link only).

link_pairs.formula: the single L/R pair is pair_index 0 (in the S/PDIF space, selected by SET_LINK space byte 0x01)
link_pairs.notes: Confirmed from capture spdif-gain-link (2026-08): SET_LINK space=0x01 / pair_index=0x00 / enabled toggled on then off. Same behaviour as the preamp/ADAT link -- while linked the Launcher sends the gain command twice (once per channel, ~1-3ms apart); the device does not propagate. Unlike ADAT, the S/PDIF link frame IS distinguishable from the physical one (space byte 0x01 vs 0x00).

buses.addressing: Output buses (monitor/headphone) are addressed with the SAME byte position as a per-input channel_offset (frame.command.channel_offset), but the value is a bus id, not a physical input index. Bus ids are NOT contiguous with each other or with channel indices -- do not assume bus id N means 'the Nth bus' in UI order.

4.name: reamp
4.notes: The Orion Studio III has TWO physical reamp outputs -- Reamp 1 and Reamp 2 (independent mono outs for driving separate guitar amps, NOT a stereo L/R pair). Capture settings-linevol-mute-reampvol-toggle exercised ONE 'Reamp' level slider (bus id 4); whether Reamp 1 and Reamp 2 share this level or have independent controls is untested.

buses.notes: Ids 3 and 4 were the settings-tab Line-output and Reamp-output levels all along, not the headphone-3/4 that the earlier guess assumed. Confirmed from capture settings-linevol-mute-reampvol-toggle (2026-08): the Launcher's 'Line' volume slider sent SET_PARAM(0x47, bus=3, level) across a full 0-96 sweep (readback at bus_block offset 37), its mute toggle sent SET_PARAM(0x48, bus=3, on/off) (readback offset 38 bit 0x04), and the 'Reamp' volume slider sent SET_PARAM(0x47, bus=4, level) (readback offset 40). So all 6 bus slots (ids 0-5) are now identified: 0=monitor_a, 1=headphone_1, 2=headphone_2, 3=line_out, 4=reamp, 5=monitor_b. bus_dim/bus_mono were not exercised on 3 or 4 and may not apply to a line/reamp output; bus_mute confirmed on 3 only.

input_mode.evidence: capture2, correlated against user action log (mode selector clicks)

gain.evidence: capture2, gain sweeps per mode, ranges match UI drag limits (not a spec sheet -- worth cross-checking)

phantom.constraint: only send when input_mode == mic; Launcher never exposes the control otherwise
phantom.evidence: capture2, never observed outside mic mode

bus_level.applies_to: buses, not input channels -- send the bus id (see 'buses') in frame.command.channel_offset
bus_level.encoding: 0 = -inf (silent) .. 96 (0x60) = 0dB / unity. Same raw 0-96 byte scale used elsewhere in this protocol (matches the resting/max value seen in gain and meter bytes), but this has only been shown to line up at the two ends (0 and 96) -- the shape of the curve in between (linear dB vs a real analog taper) is NOT confirmed.
bus_level.evidence: captures mona/monb/hp1/hp2 (2026-08): physical volume wheel dragged through its full range for buses 0, 5, 1, and 2 respectively; every SET_PARAM(0x47, bus_id, value) command in the log matched the very next state_report.bus_block reading for that bus_id. Extended in capture settings-linevol-mute-reampvol-toggle (2026-08): the settings-tab 'Line' and 'Reamp' volume sliders are SET_PARAM(0x47, bus=3) and SET_PARAM(0x47, bus=4) -- full 0-96 sweeps up and down, each matching bus_block offset 37 (bus 3) and offset 40 (bus 4) 1:1. So bus_level is now confirmed for all 6 bus ids (0-5).

bus_dim.evidence: same 4 captures, Dim button toggled on then off in isolation for each bus, matches state_report.bus_block status bit 'dim' (0x08) every time

bus_mute.evidence: captures mona/monb/hp1/hp2 (2026-08): Mute button toggled on then off in isolation for each bus, matches status bit 'mute' (0x04). Also confirmed on bus 3 in capture settings-linevol-mute-reampvol-toggle (2026-08) via the settings-tab Line-output mute toggle. Not tested on buses 4 or 5.
bus_mute.notes: The status byte's 0x04 bit is ALSO set, with no SET_PARAM(0x48) command, whenever a bus sits at bus_level == 96 (max). First seen once on bus 0 (mona capture) and thought to be a fluke; now REPRODUCED deliberately in settings-linevol-mute-reampvol-toggle (2026-08) on BOTH bus 3 and bus 4 -- the bit switches on exactly as the level sweep reaches 0x60 and switches off again on the very next step below max, every time. So bit 0x04 in the readback means 'muted OR at maximum level' and cannot distinguish the two on its own. Any bus-status readback must check bus_level: if level==96, treat 0x04 as 'at max' and report mute state as unknown/false unless a mute was explicitly sent. See unresolved_state_offsets.

bus_mono.evidence: same 4 captures, Mono button toggled on then off in isolation for each bus, matches status bit 'mono' (0x10)

output_trim.status: confirmed (3 targets; dBu scale user-confirmed 2026-09-02; RE-CONFIRMED live on the device 2026-09-03 -- swept all 3 targets, 0x73 [24]/[25] tracked value<<shift exactly, restored). Pan law: NOT param 0x4b target 3 (tested live 2026-09-03, no effect) -- still needs a Launcher capture.
output_trim.frame: command (opcode 0x13 / SET_PARAM) -- target index at offset 17, value 0-6 at offset 18

targets.0: monitor_a output trim -- CONFIRMED (capture order + dBu labels read off the Launcher, 2026-09-02)
targets.2: line_out output trim -- CONFIRMED, SAME dBu scale as the monitors (user, 2026-09-02)

output_trim.value_meaning: 7-position output-reference-level selector, 1 dBu per step: index 0 = 20 dBu, 1 = 19, 2 = 18, 3 = 17, 4 = 16, 5 = 15, 6 = 14 dBu. Same scale on all three targets (Monitor A, Monitor B, Line Out). USER-CONFIRMED against the Antelope Launcher / Orion Studio Synergy Core, 2026-09-02 -- resolves the earlier 'meaning not known from the capture'. The 2026-08 sweep covered exactly these 7 stops (0-6); the readback field is 3 bits so a value 7 is representable but the hardware offers no 8th stop.
output_trim.readback: state_report.output_trim_block -- target 0 at offset 24 (value<<4), target 1 at offset 25 bits 2-4 (value<<2), target 2 at offset 25 bits 5-7 (value<<5)
output_trim.evidence: capture settings-trim-mona-monb-line-panlaw (2026-08): each of the 3 targets swept 0->6 and back to 0; the packed readback bytes tracked value<<shift exactly on every one of the 20 steps.
output_trim.panlaw_note: The capture is named '...-panlaw' but never sent a 4th target or any other param_id -- pan law was not actually captured. TESTED LIVE 2026-09-03: SET_PARAM 0x4b target 3, values 0..3 -- zero effect on 0x73 [24]/[25], on readback cat 0x16, or anywhere. So pan law is NOT a 4th target of 0x4b. It is a different param_id (or opcode); the spare bits at 0x73 [25] bits 0-1 / [24] bits 0-3 stayed 0 throughout, so if pan law lands there it needs its own write to reveal the param. Still needs a Launcher capture (a pan-law-only click).

routing_batch_marker.frame: global_command (opcode 0x12) -- value 1 then 0 at offset 17, no target byte
routing_batch_marker.notes: Seen in macos-session-load-pre-afx-to-line (2026-08-31): every time the Launcher LOADS a preset it sends SET_GLOBAL(0x2c, 1), then the 0x53 routing frame(s) for the group(s) being changed, then SET_GLOBAL(0x2c, 0). Looks like a begin/commit marker around a batch of routing writes -- possibly an edit lock, a screen-redraw defer, or a 'session load in progress' flag. Not exercised in isolation; effect unknown. The CLI does NOT send it (single-frame route writes have worked fine on hardware without it), but a future batch `route` path could bracket its sends with it to match the Launcher.

sample_rate.frame: global_command (opcode 0x12) -- INDEX 0-6 at offset 17, no target byte. Build with build_global_command(profile, 'sample_rate', index).
sample_rate.readback: state_report offset 18 (state_report.sample_rate_byte_offset) -- the index, tracked ~1 s after the command (device clock re-lock).
sample_rate.evidence: capture macos-smplrt-32k-44k1-48-88k2-96k-176k4-192k (2026-08, native macOS): the user stepped all 7 rates in order; 7 outgoing frames op 0x12 / param 0x03 / value 0..6 at offset 17, each matched by offset 18 in a later 0x73 report, monotonic. The 3 stray op 0x13/param 0x47 frames in the file are bus-level nudges the user made to flush.
sample_rate.notes: Changing sample rate is disruptive: the device drops audio and re-locks its clock (~1 s), and if a DAW / the OS audio engine holds the stream open it may refuse or immediately revert. Best changed with nothing streaming. Same frame shape as screen_brightness (opcode 0x12). WIRED INTO cli.py (2026-08): `set-sample-rate <hz>` / `sample-rate` (status). HARDWARE ROUND-TRIP DONE 2026-09-04: every rate 44.1k..192k set and read back (offset 18 = the index; offsets 21-23 = the rate in Hz, see state_report.clock_rate_hz_offset). TWO PRECONDITIONS learned: (1) the host audio stack must not hold the USB audio interface -- on Linux `pactl set-card-profile <orion-card> off` (or stop pipewire/wireplumber) first, else every write is silently ignored (macOS releases it via CoreAudio automatically); (2) `set-sample-rate` is ALSO ignored while clock source = USB (the device defers to the host clock) -- set clock to OVEN, change the rate, then restore the clock. When clock is switched back to USB the device holds the last OVEN-set rate until the host opens the stream.

screen_brightness.frame: global_command (opcode 0x12) -- value 0-100 at offset 17, no target byte. Build with build_global_command(profile, 0x0e, value).
screen_brightness.value_meaning: Front-panel screen brightness as a percentage, 0 = off/darkest, 100 (0x64) = brightest. Raw byte == the percentage, no scaling.
screen_brightness.readback: state_report offset 26 (state_report.screen_brightness_byte_offset) -- one plain byte, equals the last commanded value.
screen_brightness.evidence: capture macos-scrbrght-0-100-50-multvalue (2026-08, native macOS): user dragged the brightness slider through 0 / 100 / 50 and many intermediate values while watching the device's physical screen change. 25 outgoing frames, all opcode 0x12 / param 0x0e / value at offset 17 (0x00..0x64); every one matched offset 26 in the next 0x73 report exactly (25/25). This overturns the earlier 'screen brightness is host-side, sends nothing' conclusion -- that was a VM artifact (the slider did nothing under the VM; the frames never reached the device). On native macOS it is a real, persisted, readable device parameter.
screen_brightness.notes: First confirmed user of opcode 0x12 with a genuine 0x73 readback (talkback params 0x1f/0x20/0x27 use 0x12 too but read back in the packed talkback_block). WIRED INTO cli.py (2026-08): `set-brightness <0-100>`, via protocol.build_global_command(profile, 'screen_brightness', value) + protocol.parse_state_scalar(profile, data, 'screen_brightness_byte_offset'). HARDWARE ROUND-TRIP CONFIRMED by the user (2026-08) -- the CLI command changes the device's physical screen.

channel_link.frame: frame.link_command (a distinct shape from every other param in this file -- NOT SET_PARAM)
channel_link.evidence: capture chlink (2026-08): all 6 pairs (index 0-5) toggled on then off in turn; frame.link_command.pair_index_offset and .enabled_offset were read directly off the wire for all 12 commands (6 on, 6 off) and matched the test sequence exactly
channel_link.side_effects: Engaging a pair's link immediately triggered fresh SET_PARAM(input_mode) and/or SET_PARAM(gain) commands for the SECOND (higher-numbered) channel of that pair -- consistent with the device syncing that channel's mode/gain to the first channel's current settings. Seen for pairs 1, 3, 4, 5 (channels ch4/ch8/ch10/ch12); not seen for pairs 0 or 2, most likely because those channels already matched, not because linking behaves differently for them. CORRECTED 2026-08 (user real-hardware test): sending ONLY the raw SET_LINK frame (opcode 0x14/param_id 0xa2) engages a real link flag on the device -- visible on the Orion's own control panel -- but the device firmware does NOT itself propagate mode/gain to the other channel; each channel keeps whatever value it already had. The mode/gain sync described above is the official Launcher software sending its own separate SET_PARAM(input_mode)/SET_PARAM(gain) commands right after the link command, not a firmware side effect of SET_LINK itself. Client software that wants Launcher-equivalent link behavior (this includes this repo's own cli.py as of 2026-08) must send that sync itself.
channel_link.live_sync_while_linked: CONFIRMED (capture ch-link-gain-ph-inv-test, 2026-08): while a pair is linked, changing gain, phantom, OR phase_invert on either channel is mirrored to the other channel on essentially every command -- gain_base_offset bytes for both channels moved in lockstep through a full ramp (offsets 49 and 50 tracking together, ~8ms apart), and status_base_offset bytes for both channels flipped together for both the phantom bit (0x10) and the phase_invert bit (0x40). This supersedes the older 'gain/mode only' note below: gain, phantom, and phase_invert all live-sync while linked. input_mode does NOT live-sync -- see mode_requires_unlink. CORRECTED 2026-08: re-examining the same ch-link-gain-ph-inv-test.tsv capture that established this shows the outgoing 0x70/0x13 frames directly -- every gain change during the linked sweep produced TWO separate outgoing SET_PARAM(gain=0x50, channel, value) frames (channel 0 then channel 1, ~2ms apart, same value), not one command with an observed two-channel effect. So "mirrored to the other channel" here means the Launcher software issued two commands, one per channel -- not that the device propagates a single write. Same conclusion as side_effects above: this is an application-layer behavior that any alternative controller (including this repo's cli.py) must replicate itself if it wants the same result; the device does not do it for you. STRONGEST CONFIRMATION (user, 2026-08): turning the PHYSICAL front-panel gain wheel on a linked channel moves ONLY that channel -- the linked partner does not follow. The hardware wheel bypasses all host software on the input path, so this proves the device firmware has zero link-propagation logic; and the Launcher evidently only mirrors changes it initiates from its own UI, not hardware-wheel changes.
channel_link.mode_requires_unlink: CONFIRMED (same capture, matches user report): input_mode cannot be changed on a linked pair -- the Launcher grays out the control. The captured workflow was unlink -> change input_mode independently per channel (status_base_offset mode bits for ch1 and ch2 changed at separate, unsynced moments, each also resetting that channel's gain to a value appropriate for the new mode's range) -> re-link. Once re-linked, subsequent phase_invert/phantom/gain changes resumed syncing across both channels immediately (no extra step needed for those three). This is expected device behavior, not a bug in the CLI or a broken link.
channel_link.notes: No 'link enabled' bit has been found yet anywhere in the 0x73 state report -- every state_report byte that changed during this capture is already fully explained by the ordinary gain_base_offset/status_base_offset formula (as a side effect, see above), not a dedicated link flag. Whether link status can be READ BACK from the device at all is unknown; the Launcher UI may just track it client-side from what it has sent. Needs a dedicated whole-report diff (link on vs off, nothing else touched) before concluding there's no readback. Independently re-verified 2026-08 directly from the raw all_reports_ch-link-gain-ph-inv-test.tsv (9362 reports): only magics 0x70/0x73/0x75 appear anywhere in the file (no hidden fourth report type), the capture's 4 link/unlink commands are all pair_index=0x00 (pair 0, ch1&ch2) alternating enabled 1/0/1/0, and diffing the 0x73 state report immediately-before vs immediately-after each of those 4 commands yields zero changed bytes every time -- actively reconfirms "no readback bit", not just "none found yet", for this capture's toggles. ITEM CLOSED 2026-09-03 -- the dedicated whole-report diff was finally done against the LIVE device: raw 0x14 link toggle on preamp pair 3 (no gain/mode sync), 0x73 read 3x keeping only bytes stable across all reads, before vs after, for BOTH on and off, plus a re-read of readback cats 0x0c / 0x15 / 0x06. Zero stable bytes moved anywhere; the readback tables were byte-identical. So: the device DOES store link state (the front panel shows it, per side_effects) but exposes it nowhere over USB HID -- not in 0x73, not in any 0x74/0x75 readback category. A controller must track link state client-side (this CLI and the Launcher both do).

adat_gain.applies_to: the 16 ADAT input channels, a separate address space from the 12 physical hybrid inputs
adat_gain.state_report_offset_formula: adat_gain_base_offset (75) + adat_channel_index (0-indexed: ADAT ch1=0 ... ADAT ch16=15)
adat_gain.evidence: capture adat-ch1-2-3-12-link12 (2026-08): gain swept individually on ADAT ch1 (offset 75), ch2 (offset 76), ch3 (offset 77), and ch12 (offset 86) -- each one-byte-per-channel offset matched 75+index exactly, and the observed value range (-6 .. +12, i.e. 0xfa..0x0c) matches the user-reported UI drag limits for ADAT gain exactly. Same layout pattern as the physical-channel gain_base_offset/status_base_offset formula, just a different base and no accompanying status byte (ADAT has no mode/phantom/phase_invert -- gain and link only). param_id CONFIRMED from the same capture's outgoing 0x70/0x13 frames: every SET_PARAM frame during the sweep used param_id=0x5b, with channel_offset (byte 17) = 0x00/0x01/0x02/0x0b for ADAT ch1/ch2/ch3/ch12 respectively -- exactly matching the readback channel-index formula, and value byte 18 sweeping the full -6..+12 range (0xfa..0x0c). Re-confirmed independently in capture ADAT-link1-2-7-8 (2026-08), same param_id=0x5b, same channel_offset formula, on ADAT ch1/ch3/ch13/ch15.
adat_gain.notes: param_id is a genuinely different value from physical-channel gain's 0x50, not a shared id -- as suspected. build_command()/build_raw_command() with param_id 0x5b and channel_offset = adat_channel_index (0-15) is now the confirmed way to set ADAT gain.

adat_channel_link.frame: frame.link_command -- same opcode (0x14)/param_id (0xa2) as physical channel_link, see notes for an important open caveat about this reuse

routing.source_encoding: Each output channel's source is TWO bytes: bank (frame.routing_command.source_banks) then index-within-bank (0-based). preamp N -> (0x00,N-1); emumic N (N = preamp number 5-12) -> (0x01,N-5); compplay N -> (0x02,N-1); ADAT N -> (0x03,N-1); S/PDIF L/R -> (0x04,0/1); AFX N -> (0x05,N-1); mix1..4 L/R -> (0x06..0x09, 0/1); surround N -> (0x0a,N-1); oscillator 1/2 -> (0x0c,0/1); mute -> (0x0b,0). Output channel c of the destination group is at bytes (19+2c, 20+2c); the whole group is always in the frame.
routing.exclusive: Routing is EXCLUSIVE per output CHANNEL -- one source per channel; a new source just overwrites that channel's (bank,idx) slot. The frame carries the whole destination group every time, so the CLI resends the channels it isn't changing -- read live from the device (frame.readback cat 0x03) before the write, and read back after. Summing multiple sources into one output is done via 'virtual mixes', a separate mechanism.
routing.readback: FOUND 2026-08-31 -- see frame.readback. It is category 0x03: one record per destination group, `<dest_id>` + a (bank,idx) pair per output channel, identical to the write frame. Verified byte-for-byte against routes the CLI wrote from Linux, and shown correctly by a fresh Windows Launcher (CAPTURE E'). `matrix-status` now does a live read. --- The text below is the SUPERSEDED pre-decode analysis (kept for the reasoning trail); its error was assuming the readback would be a HID Feature report / control transfer. It is neither -- it is an in-band 0x74-request / 0x75-response on the interrupt endpoints, and a bare 0x74 (no 10-00-00-00 sub-header) is ignored, which is why tools/readback_probe.py --poke drew a blank. --- NO USB READBACK -- as of 2026-08-31 this is close to a hard conclusion, not just 'not found'. The HID interface's report descriptor (54 bytes, dumped from Linux hidraw via tools/hid_probe.py: 06a0ff 0901 a101 0902 a100 06a1ff 0903 0904 1580257f350045ff 7508 964001 8102  0905 0906 ... 9102 c0 c0) declares EXACTLY one 320-byte Input report and one 320-byte Output report, NO Feature report, NO report IDs. The device STALLs (EPIPE) every GET_REPORT on the control pipe -- both GET_FEATURE and GET_REPORT(Input) at every length tried. So there is no HID-level readback path at all: the device only ever emits unsolicited 0x73/0x74/0x75 interrupt reports, and none of those carry routing (verified full-width, all 320 bytes, on the on2/on3 diff pair AND every matrix capture -- zero bytes track routing). The UAC2 config descriptor has no feature/selector/mixer units, so nothing routing-related is exposed there either. No vendor control request appears in ANY capture (connect, preset-LOAD, per-control). LOADING A PRESET is pure push: 0x53 routing frames bracketed by SET_GLOBAL(param 0x2c) value 1 then 0 (a batch/edit-lock marker), plus any gain frames -- the Launcher never queries the device, it writes the file's contents. CROSS-MACHINE PERSISTENCE (the original reason to think a readback existed): the device DOES store routing in NVRAM (front panel + survives power-cycle), but the cross-machine agreement the user saw is almost certainly the Antelope Launcher's own account/session sync (server-side, keyed to the logged-in account), NOT a device->host report. DECISIVE TEST STILL TO DO: change a route on the device's FRONT PANEL with no computer attached, then connect a fresh/offline Launcher -- if it shows the change there is a vendor request fired on routing-tab open (CAPTURE E', last stone); if it shows stale/default routing, there is definitively no device readback and the CLI cache is the correct and only design. CAPTURE E (macos-antelopeINIT-poweroff-on2/on3): ruled out the connect handshake -- entire host->device init is one frame SET_PARAM(0x49,ch1,0); 0x73/0x74/descriptors byte-identical between the two routings bar a preamp-gain byte + meter noise.

NO op bytes -- the old 'byte 21 = op' was a misread of the OTHER channel's (bank,idx).
