field_map.23_onward: SIXTEEN parametric EQ bands, FULLY DECODED 2026-09-03 (srrnd-EQ-Q-and-mode + srrnd-EQ-L/R-* + srrnd-EQ-L-gain). One `0x87` frame carries all 16; the Launcher shows them as 2 pages of 8. **7-byte stride, band N at [23 + 7*N] (N 0..15): `<freq LE16 Hz> <Q LE16> <gain LE16 signed> <mode byte>`.** FREQ = literal Hz, 20 .. 20000 Hz per band (user). Q = LE16, value = Q x100, range 10 (Q 0.10) .. 1800 (Q 18.0), default 0x0047 = 71 = Q 0.71 (Butterworth) -- the byte I earlier called a `0x47` marker IS the Q low byte. GAIN = LE16 signed, 0.01 dB, -2400 (-24 dB) .. +1200 (+12 dB) (user). MODE byte: `0x02` = bell (bands 2-15, always). **Bands 1 and 16 are the end-band slots** (band 1 = low end, band 16 = high end), each with TWO user modes: SHELVING and BAND-PASS (Antelope's labels; a 'flat' line in the UI is just shelf/pass at 0 gain and is NOT a separate mode). **Observed mode-byte values** -- band 1: `0x00` (rest) toggling to `0x04` (srrnd-EQ-Q-and-mode, L); band 16: `0x00` (rest) toggling `0x01` <-> `0x03` (srrnd-LFE, on the LFE strip). So the encoding is NOT a clean bitfield -- band 1 uses {0x00, 0x04}, band 16 uses {0x01, 0x03} (plus 0x00 as the untouched default). Which of the two is 'shelving' vs 'band-pass' is not yet pinned -- ask the user, they toggled it. In BOTH modes gain works and Q sets the slope. On the CENTRE channel the end bands are bell (`0x02`) only. Default freqs per page 30/120/500/1400/3000/5500/9500/14000 Hz.

family_notes._comment: Antelope Synergy Core devices share this HID protocol family (magic 0x70 command / opcode at offset 4 / param_id at 16). A peer got an Antelope Discrete 8 Pro working with it too -- see profiles/discrete_8_pro_sc.json (contributed by PR). Param IDs are shared but SEMANTICS ARE NOT guaranteed to be: value sets, encodings, ranges, and even whether a frame shape works at all can differ per device. The constraints/hazards blocks below are the safety lessons from that sibling device, applied here as precautionary defaults.
family_notes.shared_with: discrete_8_pro_sc.json (confirmed working by peer PR); discrete_4 / discrete_4_pro profiles are stubs
known_divergences_on_discrete_8_pro: input_mode 0x4f: no 'direct' mode -- value 3 CRASHES its firmware (Orion has 3=direct, confirmed here)
bus_level 0x47: encoding is plain negated dB (value N = -N dB), NOT Orion's 0-96 / 96=0dB-unity scale

gain 0x50: mic -12..65 and hiz 0..40 (vs Orion mic 0..75, hiz 0..65); line -6..20 is the same. Discrete 8 device-side CLAMPS out-of-range gain to the mode range rather than rejecting -- Orion's clamp-vs-reject behaviour is untested

channel_link (opcode 0x14 / param 0xa2): the frame shape that works on Orion does NOT link a pair on the Discrete 8 Pro, despite 0x14 being recognised -- link is the most device-specific part of the protocol
outgoing byte 0: ignored on Discrete 8 (offset 4 is the discriminator); 0x70 is cosmetic on commands
HID report descriptor: Discrete 8 has no Report ID, so Linux hidraw writes there are 321 bytes (leading 0x00 + payload) -- see transport.hidraw_write_length_unverified
error frame 0x61 ('unknown opcode') exists in the family -- see frame.error_response
min write interval ~250ms on Discrete 8 (Orion tolerates the Launcher's ~30-80ms double-sends fine)

constraints._comment: Machine-readable bounds a client should enforce before writing. Confirmed values are from Orion captures; the forbidden_opcodes and the general 'don't sweep' rule are carried from the Discrete 8 Pro, where crossing them cost a physical power cycle -- see hazards. A bound here should have a matching hazards entry explaining why.
constraints.allowed_opcodes_note: 0x53 (SET_ROUTE) and 0x17 (SET_MIX) added 2026-08 as their frame models were decoded (frame.routing_command / frame.mix_command). 0x53 is hardware round-trip confirmed (2026-08-31): preamps->hp1/hp2 and a seeded 16-ch line_out routed from cli.py persisted correctly in the Windows Launcher. 0x17 (mixer) is still untested and not in a CLI command yet -- treat the mixer as experimental. 0x1d (SET_AURAVERB) added 2026-08-31 -- all 8 DSP params decoded (frame.auraverb_command); AuraVerb is device-bundled (no per-plugin activation) so it is in scope; not hardware round-trip tested yet.
constraints.forbidden_opcodes_note: 0x01 / 0x02 = crash / unknown-dangerous (BusFault family) -- a hardware-safety block, unrelated to AFX. 0x1a / 0x1c / 0x23 added 2026-09-03 as a PRECAUTION before any AFX / Synergy Core LICENSED-plugin-chain work -- see SCOPE.md §4. This is a policy about Antelope's purchasable, activation-gated plugin catalogue (Auto-Tune, amp sims, specialized EQ/comp, etc.), NOT a stance against using the device's DSP unit in general: AuraVerb (0x1d) and the surround per-speaker EQ (readback category 0x1a, unrelated write-opcode collision) are both bundled, non-activated features and are fully decoded + in scope. Since 2026-09-04, from two macOS Launcher captures: 0x23 / param 0xd7 = the AFX SLOT-ASSIGN frame (put plugin instance <handle> on channel <ch>, or 0x00 to clear) -- see frame.afx_slot. Placing/clearing a plugin is bucket E (instantiate/load/remove), so 0x23 STAYS forbidden and build_* must never emit it; frame.afx_slot documents it for observation + readback decoding only. 0x1c / param 0xd5 = the plugin PARAMETER stream -- bucket D, frame-counted but never decoded, stays forbidden. 0x1a as a WRITE OPCODE has never been observed on this device at all -- it is blocked purely as a blanket cross-device precaution, carried over from the Zen Go profile (zen_go_sc.json), where 0x1a and 0x1c share param 0xd5 in one undecoded capture (capture_07_dsp) and 0x1a is actually a *candidate for the Zen Go's mic-modeling/emuMic frame* -- an in-scope, non-AFX feature -- not a confirmed licensed-plugin opcode. So on this device 0x1a stays forbidden as 'unconfirmed, blocked until proven safe,' not because it is known AFX/DSP content. The per-slot BYPASS toggle is a different frame (opcode 0x14 / param 0x98, bucket B, frame.afx_slot.bypass) and is NOT forbidden -- but ships no builder yet (needs a handle from the 0x0c/0x15 readback, undecoded). build_* refuses a forbidden opcode.

hazards._comment: Why the constraints above exist. Effects marked 'Discrete 8 Pro' were observed on that sibling device (peer PR); they have NOT been reproduced on Orion, but the shared protocol family and the cost of the failure mode (physical power cycle of the unit) make them precautionary defaults here. Do not treat 'not seen on Orion' as 'safe on Orion'.

blind_opcode_sweeps.rule: only send opcodes from constraints.allowed_opcodes; never a value from user input; rate-limit writes (constraints.min_write_interval_ms)
blind_opcode_sweeps.effect_on_discrete_8_pro: opcodes 0x01 and 0x02 wedged the USB controller -- every further write ETIMEDOUT, the device dropped off the bus ('device descriptor read/64, error -71'), and NEITHER a driver rebind NOR the kernel port power-cycle recovered it. Only unplugging the unit's power did.
blind_opcode_sweeps.notes: Which of 0x01/0x02 is responsible was not isolated; both forbidden. An unmapped opcode could in principle reach a routine that writes non-volatile memory or enters recalibration -- nothing observed suggests that happened, nothing rules it out. This asymmetry is the whole argument against blind sweeps, including on Orion.

channel_index_out_of_range.rule: bound-check the channel index against the RIGHT address space before writing -- constraints.channel_bounds (0-11) for gain/mode/phantom/phase, constraints.adat_channel_bounds (0-15) for adat_gain, constraints.bus_ids for bus params. Refuse, don't clamp-and-hope.
channel_index_out_of_range.effect_on_discrete_8_pro: an index above the channel count did NOT get ignored -- it raised an ARM Cortex-M BusFault ('critical error L204 busfault handler' on the panel) and needed a physical power cycle. The firmware indexes its per-channel array unchecked.
channel_index_out_of_range.notes: Orion's CLI currently only warns past channels.confirmed_indices and sends anyway. Given the sibling behaviour that is too loose -- an out-of-range write should be refused unless --force. The same byte carries bus ids for bus params, where 0-5 are legal, so a single global channel-count check is wrong.

foreign_enum_values.rule: validate every enum value against THIS profile; never pass one through from another device's profile or straight from user input
foreign_enum_values.effect_on_discrete_8_pro: input_mode = 3 (Orion's 'direct') crashed the firmware and needed a physical power cycle -- that device has no direct mode.
foreign_enum_values.notes: Orion does have input_mode 3 = direct (confirmed here), so this specific value is fine ON ORION -- the hazard is the general one: a shared profile format must not let one device's enum leak into another's code path.
